design.mixed: Existing exact control: interleaved expert/attention task IDs in one front launch, then the unchanged down/join launch.
design.blocked: Same two launches and all math; expert task IDs first, attention task IDs second within the front launch. Does NOT enforce branch serialization.
design.separate: Same expert/activation and attention tile functions in separate front launches, then the unchanged down/join launch. Three launches total.
design.serial: Same three launches as separate; attention has an extra hidden input dependency. MLX hazard tracking enforces expert-front completion before attention. No extra arithmetic or CPU evaluation barrier.
design.comparison_limit: Separate permits native MLX cross-dispatch concurrency; serial prevents it through a declared dependency. Mixed-vs-separate changes launch count and grid/resource scheduling together. Separate-vs-serial tests removal of a forced dependency, not measured hardware overlap.
